memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "But if the servant declares, 'I love my master and my wife and children and do not want to go free,' then his master must take him before the judges. He shall take him to the door or the doorpost and pierce his ear with an awl. Then he will be his servant for life." - Exodus 21:5-6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is a beautiful surprise inside a law about servants. A man who has earned his freedom may choose to stay — not because he is forced, but because he loves his master and his family. His pierced ear becomes a lifelong mark of willing, loving devotion. Freedom was his right; love made him choose to remain.

What a picture of the heart God desires! He does not want servants dragged to Him by fear or duty. He wants people who, having tasted His goodness, say from the heart, "I love my Master; I do not want to leave." Jesus took the very form of a servant for us (Phil 2:7), bound not by an awl but by nails, choosing love over freedom for our sake.

When we belong to Christ, obedience stops being a burden and becomes our joy. We serve not to earn His love but because we already have it. Is your walk with God driven by grudging obligation, or by love that keeps saying yes?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I follow God out of fear and duty, or out of love?
What would it look like to willingly bind myself to Christ today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Master, You gave Yourself fully for me. Let my obedience flow not from fear but from love, so that serving You becomes my deepest joy. Amen.
